prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" as a low-poly 3D wallpaper scene in code.

[action] Inspected ./print.jpg (the famous woodblock: giant curling wave with claw-foam crest left, three fishing boats, snow-capped Mount Fuji center-right, washi-paper sky). Built ./scene/index.html as a single file importing only three@0.170.0 from jsDelivr, everything constructed in code (no textures). Verified it renders in the browser and tuned the camera and boat placement over 3 revisions so all elements read at a glance. Wrote ./result.json. Closed the browser.

[result]
- ./scene/index.html — low-poly scene: great wave with curling crest + foam claws (left), 3 boats, Mt. Fuji (center-right), foreground swells, clouds, paper-colored background; gentle motion (wave sway, boat bob/rock, cloud drift). Flat-shaded Lambert materials, no textures, no build step.
- ./result.json — boats: 3; mountain: Mount Fuji; plus palette and assumptions.
- Evidence: browser screenshots showed the wave crest, Fuji, swells and all three boats visible in the final frame; only Google Fonts + the three.js CDN are reachable, and the file uses just the three.js import.

[how I know it is right] The image is unmistakably Hokusai's Kanagawa wave — the claw-foam crest, three funaya boats, and the small snow-capped Fuji are its signature marks, which I matched in composition, palette (indigo blues, washi paper, ochre hulls) and subjects. The scene was opened in a real browser and visually confirmed to render with all subjects present.

[assumptions] "Gentle motion" = subtle wave sway, boat bobbing, drifting clouds. Kept the print's 2D composition mapped to a shallow 3D stage (flat side-on view) so it reads as the print at a glance. No audio, no interaction beyond resize.

[open limits] Low-poly abstraction is stylized; the wave is a cone+torus approximation, not a true curling mesh. Fuji is a simple two-cone form.

Browser tabs are closed; no processes left running.
